{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Reduce forecast bias when sentiment is negative (sentiment < 0) — model tends to overestimate prices.",
    "Adjust downward for forecasts that peak sharply after a spike — model often overshoots post-spikes.",
    "Apply mean reversion correction: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10%.",
    "For sentiment = 0, use 30-day moving average as baseline to avoid overconfidence in short-term spikes.",
    "If true outcome is consistently below forecast (especially after 3–5 days), apply a 5–10% downward correction.",
    "When sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0), allow slight upward bias but cap at +5% above recent 7-day high to avoid overcorrection.",
    "Lag correction: if forecast is > 2 days ahead of true outcome, reduce by 1–2% per day to account for delayed reaction.",
    "For long-term (30-day) forecasts, apply a 3–5% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or negative."
  ]
}
